character_sheet: The Prince is the royal family's hatchling, a tiny three-headed dragon: a body with a back fin, a neck base and three two-piece necks each ending in a head with a snout, a head fin and a hinged jaw, two one-piece legs, three-panel wings a side, and a six-piece tail (ModelThePrince.createBodyLayer, ModelThePrince.java:96-171). It is a TamableAnimal with 500 HP, 0.32 speed and 10 attack (createAttributes ThePrince.java:127-135) that tames itself to the nearest player within ten blocks (:259-266) and then follows, is tempted by beef, looks about and wanders (:106-124), defending its owner and hunting monsters once tame. Its activity byte is 1 on the ground and 2 in the air (no physics when flying, :185; a 1-in-100 tick rolls a 1-in-20 flight, :274-275; it flies when hurt, when its owner flies or is far, :233-239, :279-300). On a 1-in-7 tick with a target it flies at it with the attacking flag up and bites within three blocks plus half the target's width (doHurtTarget :223-230, counting its kills) or, between five and twelve blocks with its fire lit and its head aimed, fires a fireball, a thunderbolt or an ice ball from three blocks ahead (doMovement :358-403, firecanon / firecanonl / firecanoni :482-552); a tamed one below a quarter health flees. Its three necks rise and fall on synced extensions (0 to 60, random-walked, :187-202). After 25 kills, 10 feedings and 10 days it grows into the Prince Teen (:305, transformToTeen :553-560); a diamond block heals it and clears it to grow, a diamond grows it (:616-634), ice and flint and steel take and give its fire (:661-677). It spawns wherever it is placed (checkSpawnRules :750-753; no biome file names it). Read it as a hatchling: quick little wing-beats, three bobbing heads, a tail that wags.
size_notes: Drawn at x0.75 of the rig (ThePrinceRenderer.java:20, applied :30; shadow 0.75 x 0.75) on a 128x128 sheet (ModelThePrince.java:171); 0.75 x 1.25 block hitbox (ModEntities.java:574-575). The design's row warns the small targets may fail usability testing and would then be demoted to Tier 2 rather than inflated. The tail and the necks are chains the code positions segment by segment — key the joints, never the positions.

groups.name: gait
groups.amplitude: pi x 0.25 = 0.785 rad (45 deg) x the walking speed above a 0.1 threshold (zero below it), the right leg + and the left −; in flight (activity 2) and not attacking both legs are held tucked at −1 rad
groups.plain: the two little legs stride with the walking speed on the ground and tuck up in flight
groups.math: a = amount > 0.1 ? cos(t * 2.0 * 0.65) * pi * 0.25 * amount : 0; (activity != 2 || attacking) ? (Rleg1.xRot = a, Lleg1.xRot = -a) : (Rleg1.xRot = Lleg1.xRot = -1)
groups.phase: the synced DATA_ACTIVITY byte (ThePrince.java:63; 2 in flight) selects the tuck unless the attacking flag is set
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 2.0 x wingspeed 0.65 = 1.3 rad/tick: the natural period is 4.83 ticks

groups.name: wings
groups.amplitude: moving (speed above 0.1) or attacking: pi x 0.4 = 1.257 rad (72 deg) x the walking speed at 1.495 rad/tick; still: pi x 0.04 = 0.126 rad (7 deg) at 0.195 rad/tick; the right panels about −0.4 / −0.6 / −0.2, the left the negative wave about +0.4 / +0.6 / +0.2
groups.plain: the wings beat fast and wide with the speed or when attacking, and stir slowly at rest
groups.math: w = (amount > 0.1 || attacking) ? cos(t * 2.3 * 0.65) * pi * 0.4 * amount : cos(t * 0.3 * 0.65) * pi * 0.04; Rwing.zRot = w - 0.4; Rwing2.zRot = w - 0.6; Rwing3.zRot = w - 0.2; Lwing.zRot = -w + 0.4; Lwing2.zRot = -w + 0.6; Lwing3.zRot = -w + 0.2
groups.phase: state-branching: the speed threshold or the attacking flag selects the fast beat (note the beat is still scaled by the walking speed while attacking: a hovering attacker's wings are nearly still in the code)
groups.omega_note: the classic phase moving is ageInTicks x 2.3 x wingspeed 0.65 = 1.495 rad/tick (period 4.2 ticks); still 0.3 x 0.65 = 0.195 (32.2 ticks)

groups.name: tail
groups.amplitude: calm: pi x 0.06 = 0.188 rad (11 deg) at 0.585 rad/tick; attacking: pi x 0.12 = 0.377 rad (22 deg) at 0.845 rad/tick; zero when sitting; scaled 1 / 1.6 / 2.6 / 3.6 / 4.6 along segments 2 to 6, each placed at the end of the one before
groups.plain: the tail wags, the swing growing toward the tip — faster and wider while attacking, still when sitting
groups.math: g = sitting ? 0 : (attacking ? cos(t * 1.3 * 0.65) * pi * 0.12 : cos(t * 0.9 * 0.65) * pi * 0.06); tail2.yRot = g; tail3 = 1.6g; tail4 = 2.6g; Tail5 = 3.6g; Tail6 = 4.6g; positions along the chain
groups.phase: isOrderedToSit stills it; the attacking flag selects the fast wave
groups.omega_note: the classic phase calm is ageInTicks x 0.9 x wingspeed 0.65 = 0.585 rad/tick (period 10.7 ticks); attacking 1.3 x 0.65 = 0.845 (7.4 ticks)

groups.name: jaws
groups.amplitude: attacking: pi x 0.2 = 0.628 rad (36 deg) about 0.2 plus the head's pitch, each jaw on its own rate — the left at 1.9 x 0.65 = 1.235 rad/tick, the right at 2.1 x 0.65 = 1.365, the centre at 2.3 x 0.65 = 1.495; not attacking: the head's pitch only
groups.plain: the three jaws chomp on three slightly different rates while the attacking flag is set
groups.math: Ljx = attacking ? 0.2 + cos(t * 1.9 * 0.65) * pi * 0.2 : 0; Rjx = attacking ? 0.2 + cos(t * 2.1 * 0.65) * pi * 0.2 : 0; jx = attacking ? 0.2 + cos(t * 2.3 * 0.65) * pi * 0.2 : 0; Ljaw.xRot = pitch_L + Ljx; jaw.xRot = pitch_C + jx; Rjaw.xRot = pitch_R + Rjx
groups.phase: the synced DATA_ATTACKING byte (ThePrince.java:67, set at :373 with a target, cleared at :365 / :405) selects
groups.omega_note: the classic phases are ageInTicks x 1.9 / 2.1 / 2.3 x wingspeed 0.65 = 1.235 / 1.365 / 1.495 rad/tick (periods 5.1 / 4.6 / 4.2 ticks)

behaviour: The two little legs stride 45 degrees at top speed at 1.3 rad/tick above a walking-speed threshold of 0.1, and tuck up at −1 rad in flight unless it is attacking (ModelThePrince.java:189-198; the activity byte is ThePrince.java:63, 2 in the air).

The wings beat 72 degrees x the walking speed at 1.495 rad/tick (a 4.2-tick beat) when it moves or the attacking flag is set, and stir 7 degrees at 0.195 otherwise (:179-187) — the beat is scaled by the walking speed even in flight, so a hovering Prince's wings barely move in the code. The tail wags along five segments, the tip 4.6 times the root — 11 degrees at 0.585 rad/tick at rest, 22 at 0.845 attacking, still when sitting (:200-219).

The three heads share the look: two thirds of the look yaw and pitch go to the heads on the side the look turns to and half of that to the others, each upper neck half its head's yaw (:221-256, :270-281); the lower necks pitch by the three synced head extensions, which random-walk between 0 and 60 degrees (ThePrince.java:187-202; ModelThePrince.java:283-288). The jaws chomp 36 degrees on three rates while attacking (:258-268).
The body, back fin, neck base and tail base are static; the snouts and head fins ride their heads.

The bite (doHurtTarget, ThePrince.java:223-230), the canon trio (:482-552) and the growth into the Teen (:553-560) are rolled by doMovement and customServerAiStep — nothing in the code fires an animation for them.

wishlist: in `fly`: a proper hover beat — the code's wing beat is scaled by the walking speed (ModelThePrince.java:180), so a hovering Prince's wings barely move; give it a quick wide flutter and a body bob
in `walk`: a scamper — the code swings the two legs 45 degrees (:189-194); add a waddle of the body and the tail's wag (:200-219)
in `attack`: a three-headed nip with the jaws' chomp (:258-268); the bite lands within three blocks plus half the target's width (ThePrince.java:377-380)
in `idle`: keep the three heads bobbing on their extensions (ThePrince.java:187-202) — each head on its own timing — so it reads as curious
locked_bones_note: The design's section 6 ModelThePrince row (geckolib_migration_design.md:454): 'head/Lhead/Rhead [0.35,0.35] @1; body [0.7,0.55] @0.5; Lleg1/Rleg1 [0.22,0.5] @0.5; Lwing/Rwing [0.55,0.2] @0.25; tail1/tail4 [0.25,0.35] @0.25'. Every design name resolves to the port model's part names as written (ModelThePrince.createBodyLayer). The row: 'Small targets may fail usability testing; if so demote to Tier 2 instead of inflating boxes beyond the art.'
formulas: `ModelThePrince.poseFrom` (ModelThePrince.java:183-318; orig ModelThePrince.java:274-430 in `render` (func_78088_a, :268-433; func_78087_a at :441-443 is a bare super call), wingspeed 0.65 from `new ModelThePrince(0.65f)` in orig ClientProxyOreSpawn.java:494 - the port's WINGSPEED): while the walking speed is above a tenth or the entity is attacking the wing angle is the cosine of the age in ticks times 2.3 times the wingspeed, times pi, times 0.4, times the walking speed, else the cosine of the age times 0.3 times the wingspeed, times pi, times 0.04: the three right wing parts roll by it minus 0.4, 0.6 and 0.2, the three left by its negative plus 0.4, 0.6 and 0.2. While the walking speed is above a tenth the leg swing is the cosine of the age times 2.0 times the wingspeed, times pi, times 0.25, times the walking speed, else 0; unless the activity is 2 with the entity not attacking, the right leg pitches by it and the left by its negative; otherwise both pitch -1.0. The tail angle is the cosine of the age times 0.9 times the wingspeed, times pi, times 0.06, or 0 while ordered to sit, or attacking the cosine of the age times 1.3 times the wingspeed, times pi, times 0.12: the second tail part yaws by it, the third by 1.6 times it placed 6 units from the second along the cosine (z) and sine (x) of the second's yaw, the fourth by 2.6 times placed 5 units on, the fifth by 3.6 times placed 4 on, the sixth by 4.6 times placed 4 on. The head look is split three ways: two thirds of the look yaw on the centre head and half of that on the side heads on the side the head turns to (the left heads when the yaw is negative, else the right), the same for the pitch - each head's head, snout, fin and jaw yaw and pitch by its share in radians and its neck yaws by half the share; attacking, the three jaws add 0.2 plus the cosine of the age times 1.9 (the left), 2.1 (the right) and 2.3 (the centre) times the wingspeed, times pi, times 0.2. The three necks pitch by the entity's head extensions in degrees (0 at rest) and each head group (head, jaw, snout, fin) is placed 7 units from its neck's pivot - down the cosine of the neck's pitch, back along its sine and across by the product of the sines of its yaw and pitch. The classic's early jaw writes from the snout's position before the frame are overwritten by that follow (dead writes, transcribed as such). The walk position plays no part. The GeckoLib hook is the same (ThePrinceGeoReplacement.applyCustomAnimations).
